title: The category of formal coproducts (semi-representable objects) of a category
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category. The *category of formal coproducts* (semi-representable objects) $\mathrm{SR}(\mathcal C)$ has as objects the families $\{U_i\}_{i\in I}$ of objects of $\mathcal C$ indexed by a set $I$. A morphism $\{U_i\}_{i\in I}\to\{V_j\}_{j\in J}$ is a pair $(\alpha,(f_i)_{i\in I})$ of a map $\alpha:I\to J$ and morphisms $f_i:U_i\to V_{\alpha(i)}$ of $\mathcal C$; the identity of $\{U_i\}_{i\in I}$ is $(\mathrm{id}_I,(\mathrm{id}_{U_i})_i)$, and composition is $(\beta,(g_j)_{j\in J})\circ(\alpha,(f_i)_{i\in I})=(\beta\circ\alpha,(g_{\alpha(i)}\circ f_i)_{i\in I})$. For an object $T$ of $\mathcal C$, $\{T\}$ denotes the one-member family (indexed by a one-point set), and $T\mapsto\{T\}$, $h\mapsto(\mathrm{id},(h))$ is a functor $\mathcal C\to\mathrm{SR}(\mathcal C)$. A morphism $\{T\}\to\{V_j\}_{j\in J}$ is the same as a pair $(j,t)$ of an index $j\in J$ and a morphism $t:T\to V_j$ of $\mathcal C$.
